paragraphs: Multimodal language models process images through visual tokens, and using many of these tokens throughout training can be expensive. Chain-of-Sight introduces a bridge between vision and language that lets pre-training use fewer visual tokens while allowing fine-tuning to use substantially more. The approach makes the amount of visual detail processed adjustable across training stages.

The bridge contains a sequence of visual resamplers that capture information at different spatial scales. This gives the model access to both the overall image and smaller details. A compound token scaling strategy then expands the visual token count after pre-training, with increases of up to sixteen times supported by the architecture.

In the reported experiments, reducing visual tokens during pre-training cut elapsed training time by approximately 73%. Across the evaluated vision-language benchmarks, performance matched or exceeded a pipeline that used all visual tokens throughout training. The authors also report stronger results when allocating more tokens to pre-training, showing that the design supports different balances between training expense and performance.
neurips-2024-accelerating-pre-training-o.tldr: Chain-of-Sight reduces pre-training time by using fewer visual tokens early and expanding them later, while maintaining performance in the reported benchmarks.

paragraphs: Relative entropy coding communicates a random sample drawn from a target distribution using another distribution already shared by the sender and receiver. Its practical difficulty is encoding time: general algorithms require work that grows at least exponentially with the divergence between these two distributions. A larger mismatch can therefore make an otherwise useful compression approach too slow.

The paper introduces a coding scheme that partitions the sample space to reduce runtime in practical settings. The central change is how the coding problem is organized, with space partitioning providing a way to make harder distribution pairs more manageable. The authors support the method with theoretical analysis, simple examples, and neural compression applications.

In the reported evaluations, the method handles distribution divergences roughly three times larger than previous methods could manage. It also reduces bitrate by approximately 5–15% in the tested lossless MNIST and lossy CIFAR-10 compression applications. These results support improved practical reach and compression efficiency in those settings; the abstract does not claim to eliminate the general exponential encoding difficulty.
neurips-2024-accelerating-relative-entro.tldr: Space partitioning makes relative entropy coding practical for larger distribution mismatches and improves bitrate in the tested neural compression applications.

paragraphs: Lower bounds describe limits that no learning algorithm can overcome within a specified problem. Classical techniques provide powerful results for statistical estimation, but interactive learning introduces another difficulty: an algorithm's decisions determine which data it receives. Existing bounds based on the Decision-Estimation Coefficient capture this interaction, yet do not recover the strongest known bounds for passive estimation.

The paper develops an interactive Fano method that connects these approaches within one framework. It also introduces a complexity measure called the Fractional Covering Number. This measure brings estimation difficulty into lower bounds for interactive decision making, extending the perspective supplied by the Decision-Estimation Coefficient.

The framework yields a unified characterization of whether any stochastic bandit problem is learnable. It also closes a remaining gap between earlier upper and lower bounds, up to polynomial factors, for interactive decision problems whose underlying model class is convex. The convexity condition and polynomial qualification define the scope of that second result. The contribution is a common way to reason about fundamental difficulty across passive estimation and adaptive data collection.
neurips-2024-assouad-fano-and-le-cam-wit.tldr: An interactive Fano framework unifies estimation and decision-making lower bounds and provides a general characterization of stochastic bandit learnability.

paragraphs: BricksRL makes physical robot learning more accessible by connecting custom LEGO robots to reinforcement learning software. Its purpose is to support research and teaching with inexpensive, configurable hardware that users can build and train in the real world. The platform includes robot construction plans and training results across several tasks and configurations.

The technical connection runs through TorchRL and two-way Bluetooth communication with LEGO hubs. This supplies the communication infrastructure linking the robot, its environment, and the learning algorithm, while allowing reinforcement learning training on GPUs. Because the interface supports different LEGO builds, users can explore multiple robot designs within the same software framework.

The experiments show that inexpensive LEGO robots can learn simple tasks through end-to-end training on physical hardware, typically in under 120 minutes using a normal laptop. The authors also demonstrate integration with sensors from outside the LEGO ecosystem. Together, these findings show a practical route to adaptable robotics experiments and classroom activities, with the stated training-time result applying to the simple tasks demonstrated.
neurips-2024-bricksrl-a-platform-for-dem.tldr: BricksRL connects LEGO robots to TorchRL, enabling inexpensive real-world learning experiments with simple tasks typically trained in under two hours.

paragraphs: High-quality 3D reconstruction often depends on collecting hundreds or thousands of photographs of a scene. CAT3D reduces this capture burden by generating additional views computationally. It treats image generation as a way to simulate the photographs that a reconstruction system would otherwise need a person to collect.

The method uses a multi-view diffusion model that receives input images and a set of requested camera viewpoints. It generates views intended to remain highly consistent with one another, which matters because they must describe the same scene from different positions. These generated images then become inputs to robust 3D reconstruction techniques.

The resulting 3D representations support real-time rendering from arbitrary viewpoints. The authors report creating entire scenes in as little as one minute and outperforming existing methods for scene creation from a single image or a few views. The timing is a best-case capability stated in the abstract, rather than a universal runtime. The central contribution is connecting coherent view generation to reconstruction so that scene creation requires less manual image capture.
neurips-2024-cat3d-create-anything-in-3d.tldr: CAT3D generates consistent additional viewpoints from input images and uses them to reconstruct 3D scenes, sometimes in as little as one minute.

paragraphs: ConceptFactory aims to make annotations of 3D object knowledge easier to produce and customize. Its organizing idea is object conceptualization: describing objects through arrangements of general geometric components, such as cuboids and cylinders. The authors draw this approach from research suggesting that human object recognition can be understood in terms of such components.

The contribution has two parts. ConceptFactory Suite provides a web-based annotation platform driven by a Standard Concept Template Library. ConceptFactory Asset supplies a large collection of objects already represented through these concepts. Together, the tools and collection give researchers a shared basis for acquiring different kinds of object knowledge and adapting that knowledge to their own tasks.

The authors evaluate the annotations across benchmark tasks involving both vision and robotics, using state-of-the-art algorithms. They report evidence of annotation quality and versatility across these uses. The broader value is that a common conceptual description can support multiple forms of object understanding, making the annotation process useful beyond a single narrowly defined task.
neurips-2024-conceptfactory-facilitate-3.tldr: ConceptFactory uses reusable geometric concepts, a web toolbox, and an object collection to support versatile 3D knowledge annotation.

paragraphs: Protein language models contain information shaped by evolution, but protein optimization often targets one particular property. Evolution reflects multiple functional demands at once, so the information useful for the desired property can be mixed with information that distracts from it. Property measurements also depend on experimental conditions, complicating generalization to unfamiliar proteins.

DePLM treats evolutionary information as a mixture of relevant signal and task-specific noise. It refines that information through a diffusion process applied in the rank space of property values. Working with ranks makes the ordering of property values central to the learning process. The authors present this design as a way to support dataset-agnostic learning and improve generalization.

The experiments report performance beyond the compared state of the art on mutation effect prediction, alongside strong generalization to novel proteins. These findings support the idea that evolutionary information becomes more useful for a particular optimization objective when irrelevant components are filtered out. The reported evidence concerns prediction and generalization, which are computational ingredients for deciding which sequence changes may improve a protein.
neurips-2024-deplm-denoising-protein-lan.tldr: DePLM denoises evolutionary information in protein language models to improve mutation effect prediction and generalization to novel proteins.

paragraphs: Director3D addresses text-driven 3D generation using real-world captures, where camera motion is more complex and scene-dependent than the predefined trajectories common in synthetic datasets. Its framework generates both a scene and a camera trajectory suited to the text. This makes camera movement part of the generation problem rather than a fixed input chosen independently.

The system divides the work into three stages. A trajectory diffusion transformer first generates camera motion from the description. A multi-view latent diffusion model then produces an image sequence conditioned on that motion and the text. This second model directly generates pixel-aligned 3D Gaussians, providing an immediate scene representation that supports consistency during denoising.

A final stage refines those Gaussians with the proposed SDS++ loss, drawing on knowledge from a 2D diffusion model. The authors report that Director3D outperforms existing methods in their real-world 3D generation experiments. The approach matters because it connects scene-specific camera trajectories, coordinated image generation, and explicit 3D refinement within one framework designed to exploit real-world data.
neurips-2024-director3d-real-world-camer.tldr: Director3D jointly generates text-conditioned camera trajectories and 3D scenes, then refines the scenes using a 2D diffusion model.

paragraphs: Large-vocabulary object detectors can locate objects across many categories, yet recognizing those objects becomes difficult when downstream images or category vocabularies differ from training. This paper targets that gap between finding an object and assigning it the right identity. It draws on CLIP's open-vocabulary recognition knowledge to adapt an existing detector to downstream domains.

The proposed Knowledge Graph Distillation method first represents downstream data using CLIP. Data representations become graph nodes, and distances between their features define graph edges. This exposes semantic relationships carried implicitly by CLIP. A second stage transfers the extracted graph into the detector to improve classification across domains.

The method can extract visual and textual graphs separately, supplying complementary information for localization and classification. Across multiple established detection benchmarks, the authors report consistently large improvements over the compared state of the art. The contribution is a structured transfer mechanism: adaptation uses relationships among representations to bring recognition knowledge into a detector facing different data and object vocabularies.
neurips-2024-domain-adaptation-for-large.tldr: Knowledge Graph Distillation transfers CLIP's visual and textual relationships into object detectors to improve recognition in new domains.

paragraphs: An agent with several distinct skills has more ways to explore its environment. LEADS formalizes the goal of learning skills that collectively cover the state space uniformly. It builds on an earlier formulation using mutual information between skills and states, asking how each skill changes the distribution of places the agent reaches.

The method uses successor state representations to describe states reached under a policy conditioned on a particular skill. It then maximizes differences between the resulting distributions. This makes diversity a property of where skills take the agent, linking the skill-learning objective directly to coverage of the environment.

In maze navigation and robotic control experiments, the authors report learning diverse skills that exhaustively cover the tested state spaces without relying on rewards or exploration bonuses. They also describe more robust and efficient exploration through combining mutual information maximization with exploration bonuses. These statements distinguish the demonstrated ability to construct coverage-producing skills without bonuses from the broader exploration benefits discussed for combining objectives.
neurips-2024-exploration-by-learning-div.tldr: LEADS learns diverse skills by separating their future-state distributions, achieving broad exploration in the tested navigation and robotic control tasks.

paragraphs: This paper studies classification with limited feedback: after predicting one of K labels, a learner hears only whether its answer was correct. The agnostic setting allows the candidate predictors to be imperfect. The goal is to approach the best available predictor with a specified accuracy and confidence while using as few examples as possible.

For finite hypothesis classes, the new algorithm gives a sample bound with a polynomial-in-K term added to a term proportional to one over squared error tolerance. Earlier bounds multiplied that accuracy term by K. The authors extend their result to general classes using Natarajan dimension, a measure of multiclass hypothesis complexity.

As the error tolerance approaches zero, the multiplicative cost of limited feedback is only constant order in this agnostic setting, contrasting with the K-dependent cost established for realizable learning. The algorithm constructs a low-variance exploration distribution using stochastic optimization, a log-barrier potential, and Frank-Wolfe updates. Its computational efficiency is conditional on access to an empirical risk minimization oracle over the hypothesis class.
neurips-2024-fast-rates-for-bandit-pac-m.tldr: A new bandit-feedback classifier removes the multiplicative label-count penalty from the leading accuracy-dependent sample bound in agnostic learning.

paragraphs: Simulations of molecular and related stochastic systems can spend long periods trapped in metastable states because high barriers make transitions rare. Biasing a simulation helps it explore faster, but the resulting data describe altered dynamics. This paper asks how to recover spectral information about the original system from those biased observations.

The framework applies to time-reversal invariant stochastic processes, including Langevin dynamics. It learns through the process's infinitesimal generator and associated resolvent operator. These provide an alternative to methods based on a transfer operator. The authors establish that their approach can recover spectral properties of the unbiased system from biased data.

Experiments show advantages over the compared transfer-operator and generator-learning approaches when estimating eigenfunctions and eigenvalues. The authors also recover relevant information about transition mechanisms from datasets containing only a few useful transitions because the biasing was suboptimal. This result matters when faster exploration still leaves transitions sparsely observed: the method can extract useful dynamical information in the demonstrated cases, within the paper's stated class of processes.
neurips-2024-from-biased-to-unbiased-dyn.tldr: A generator-based framework recovers unbiased spectral dynamics from biased simulations, including tested cases with few relevant transitions.

paragraphs: GTA evaluates whether language-model agents can solve practical problems using tools. The authors argue that evaluations built around synthetic queries, single actions, simulated tools, or text alone miss important demands of actual use. Their benchmark instead combines human-written requests, deployed tools, and image-based context within tasks requiring executable solutions.

The requests describe relatively simple user goals without spelling out which tools to use. Agents must identify suitable tools and plan the required steps. The platform includes tools for perception, operation, logic, and creativity, while inputs include spatial scenes, webpage screenshots, tables, code snippets, and printed or handwritten material.

The benchmark contains 229 tasks with executable tool chains. In the reported evaluation, GPT-4 completes fewer than half of the tasks, and most evaluated models complete fewer than a quarter. These results show that successful tool use remains difficult when choosing tools, interpreting multimodal context, and executing a plan are combined. GTA provides a way to assess that overall problem-solving ability through actual task completion.
neurips-2024-gta-a-benchmark-for-general.tldr: GTA tests agents on 229 human-written tasks with real tools and multimodal inputs, revealing low completion rates among the evaluated models.

paragraphs: IR-CM targets image restoration with very few inference steps, including a single step. It builds consistency distillation or training around a particular mean-reverting stochastic differential equation. The aim is to obtain a general image-to-image transformation method that can restore degraded images without requiring a long sequence of inference operations.

The authors introduce a training strategy that separates linear and nonlinear components. They report that this improves training effectiveness and inference performance compared with consistency distillation. The strategy also allows training independently of a pretrained checkpoint. An additional origin-guided loss helps avoid trivial solutions and stabilize the learning process.

The evaluation covers removing rain, reducing noise, correcting blur, and enhancing low-light images. One-step inference produces highly competitive results across the reported experiments, while two-step inference reaches the reported state of the art for low-light enhancement. Ablation experiments support the training strategy's contribution. These findings make the training design central to the method: efficient restoration depends on learning a useful short inference process, with the strongest stated task-specific result using two steps.
neurips-2024-ir-cm-the-fast-and-general-.tldr: IR-CM enables competitive one-step image restoration through consistency training, with two-step state-of-the-art results reported for low-light enhancement.

paragraphs: SpatialEval examines how well language and vision-language models understand spatial relationships, navigate, and count. These abilities are central to interpreting arrangements and moving through them, yet the authors identify spatial reasoning as underexplored relative to broader model performance. The benchmark brings several aspects of this capability into a common evaluation.

The findings challenge the expectation that additional visual information will reliably help. Competitive models can score below random guessing on spatial reasoning tasks, and vision-language models often perform worse than their language-only counterparts. When adequate textual clues accompany an image, multimodal models also become less dependent on the visual information.

The authors demonstrate that using redundancy between text and vision can significantly improve performance. This suggests that the way overlapping information is presented or used matters alongside the availability of an image. The study therefore identifies both a weakness and an opportunity: spatial competence remains difficult for the evaluated models, while coordinated use of text and visual evidence can improve their results.
neurips-2024-is-a-picture-worth-a-thousa.tldr: SpatialEval reveals substantial spatial-reasoning weaknesses and shows that visual input alone does not reliably improve model performance.

paragraphs: State space models propagate information recursively and can provide strong representations efficiently. The paper argues that organizing this propagation along a sequence restricts how well distant inputs interact. MambaTree changes the structure over which features move, aiming to improve long-range dependencies while retaining the computational appeal of state space modeling.

For each input, the network dynamically constructs a tree using spatial relationships and input features. It then propagates features along that tree, moving beyond the original sequence geometry. A dynamic programming algorithm performs the computation with linear complexity, supporting stronger long-range interactions without increasing the computational cost as described by the authors.

The framework applies to both images and text. Experiments report significant improvements over existing structured state space models in image classification, object detection, and segmentation. Fine-tuning large language models with the approach also produces consistent gains across multiple text tasks at a small training cost. The results support changing information-flow structure as a useful design choice across the evaluated modalities.
neurips-2024-mambatree-tree-topology-is-.tldr: MambaTree propagates features through an input-dependent tree to improve long-range interactions while retaining linear computational complexity.

paragraphs: This paper studies whether weaker language models can judge stronger models more accurately through structured interaction. It compares debate between two agents, consultancy with one agent answering a judge's questions, and direct answering by the judge. Weaker models serve as stand-ins for human judges across information, mathematical, coding, logical, and multimodal reasoning asymmetries.

When consultants are randomly assigned to defend correct or incorrect answers, debate outperforms consultancy across all evaluated tasks. Its advantage over direct answering is more conditional. Debate helps in extractive question answering where agents and judges have unequal information, but results are mixed on other tasks without that information asymmetry.

When agents choose their own answers to defend, judges are less often persuaded by an incorrect answer in debate than in consultancy. Stronger debaters also improve judge accuracy, though the gains are more modest than in earlier studies. These findings support debate relative to consultancy in the tested settings, while showing that its value over a judge working alone depends on the task and information available.
neurips-2024-on-scalable-oversight-with-.tldr: Debate improves weaker judges' decisions relative to consultancy in the tested settings, but its advantage over direct answering depends on the task.

paragraphs: Human preferences have multiple dimensions, and reducing them to one scalar label can obscure important tradeoffs. Panacea treats language-model alignment as optimization over a vector of preferences. It trains one model whose behavior can adapt to different preference settings at use time, without additional tuning for each setting.

The challenge is connecting a small preference vector to a model with many parameters. Panacea uses low-rank adaptation based on singular value decomposition, inserting preference values as singular values during use. This provides a direct mechanism for controlling the trained model through a compact preference representation.

The authors prove that, under mild conditions and common loss aggregation methods, Panacea recovers the entire Pareto front: the set of tradeoffs where improving one objective requires sacrificing another. Experiments demonstrate a single model representing an exponentially large range of preferences under several optimization methods. The theoretical claim remains conditional on its stated assumptions, while the experiments support the feasibility of broad preference adaptation within one trained model.
neurips-2024-panacea-pareto-alignment-vi.tldr: Panacea trains one language model to adapt to multidimensional preferences without further tuning, with conditional guarantees of recovering the Pareto front.

paragraphs: Generative AI pricing involves a model that can serve many tasks through repeated prompts, with success judged by whether users are satisfied. This paper first compares two models by user cost-effectiveness on a particular task. It then studies competition between two companies that release their models sequentially before users select a model for each task.

Within this game, pricing involves choosing which tasks to compete for. A company may set a price that makes its model cost-effective on some tasks while giving up revenue from others. The resulting optimization is piecewise continuous, reflecting changes in which tasks a particular price can attract.

The analysis shows that a later entrant who knows its competitor's price can always secure cost-effectiveness on at least one task within the model. The first entrant must account for how its price influences the later company's choice. When tasks are sufficiently similar, the first model may be cost-ineffective on every task regardless of its price. These are conditional economic-model findings about information and timing, rather than unconditional predictions about all AI markets.
neurips-2024-pricing-and-competition-for.tldr: A sequential pricing model shows how knowing a competitor's price can benefit later generative-AI entrants and, under certain conditions, undermine first movers.

paragraphs: Changing an image's aspect ratio can damage its content: important objects may disappear or become distorted, and local edits can leave visible discontinuities. PruneRepaint addresses this by treating resizing as a content-sensitive editing problem. It aims to preserve the image's key meaning while maintaining a visually coherent result.

The method assigns semantic importance to individual pixels to guide which regions should be removed and which should remain. After pruning, an adaptive module selects areas to repaint. That selection depends on where pixels were removed and on the relationship between foreground size and the requested aspect ratio, allowing repairs to respond to the particular edit.

Experiments on RetargetMe, including objective evaluations and user studies, report better preservation of meaning and aesthetics than previous approaches. The authors also report better generalization across diverse aspect ratios. The approach matters because content preservation and visual repair are coordinated: decisions about what to remove help determine where repainting is needed to reduce artifacts and protect foreground structure.
neurips-2024-prune-and-repaint-content-a.tldr: PruneRepaint changes image aspect ratios by preserving semantically important content and adaptively repairing regions affected by pixel removal.

paragraphs: Medical image grading is difficult because disease severity changes continuously: cases within one grade can vary, while adjacent grades can look similar. Performance can deteriorate further when a model encounters images from an unseen domain. Samba addresses both challenges by organizing image processing around severity information and recalibrating features affected by domain differences.

The method processes image patches sequentially with a state space model whose hidden states store and carry severity information. This reflects the authors' observation that the most severe lesions can determine staging while occupying only a small image region. An expectation-maximization mechanism then maps patch representations into a more compact space.

Samba models lesion feature distributions with a Gaussian mixture model and reconstructs intermediate features using learnable severity bases. The authors report average accuracy improvements over VMamba of 23.5%, 5.6%, and 4.1% for cross-domain grading of fatigue fracture, breast cancer, and diabetic retinopathy, respectively. These experimental findings support the combined use of severity-sensitive information propagation and feature recalibration for the evaluated grading tasks.
neurips-2024-samba-severity-aware-recurr.tldr: Samba carries lesion severity across image patches and recalibrates features to improve medical image grading across unseen domains.

paragraphs: Inferring a dynamical system's structure means identifying the interactions underlying its observed behavior. This becomes harder when measurements arrive at irregular intervals or some parts of the system remain unobserved. SICSM addresses these conditions by combining selective state space models for temporal learning with Generative Flow Networks for structural inference.

The state space component learns input-dependent transition functions that adapt to unequal time intervals. It aggregates information across different temporal dependencies and passes that information to the Generative Flow Network. The resulting framework approximates a posterior distribution over system structures, representing plausible interaction patterns rather than only producing a single structural guess.

The approach also incorporates prior knowledge into inference. Across sixteen datasets, the authors report better performance than existing methods, especially under irregular sampling and incomplete observation. These findings support the combination of adaptable temporal modeling and probabilistic structural inference in the evaluated settings. The proposed applications include scientific discovery and system diagnostics, where identifying relationships from imperfect time-series measurements is an important part of understanding complex systems.
neurips-2024-structural-inference-of-dyn.tldr: SICSM combines selective state space models and Generative Flow Networks to infer system structures from irregular and partially observed trajectories.

paragraphs: Text-to-video diffusion models produce videos through repeated sampling steps, which can make generation slow. Consistency models shorten that process but can lose quality. T2V-Turbo aims to improve the quality of fast video generation by adding feedback from several differentiable reward models while distilling a pretrained text-to-video model.

The method optimizes rewards on single-step generations that already arise when computing the consistency distillation loss. This allows reward feedback to influence training without propagating gradients through an entire iterative sampling sequence. The design therefore addresses a memory constraint that would otherwise complicate reward-based optimization of video generation.

The authors report that four-step T2V-Turbo generation achieves the highest total VBench score in their comparison, including scores above Gen-2 and Pika. Human evaluations also prefer its four-step outputs over the teacher models' fifty-step DDIM samples. In those comparisons, the method combines improved video quality with more than tenfold acceleration. The findings support using mixed reward feedback during distillation to improve the quality available from a short generation process.
neurips-2024-t2v-turbo-breaking-the-qual.tldr: T2V-Turbo adds mixed reward feedback to consistency distillation, producing four-step videos preferred over its teachers' fifty-step samples in human evaluations.

paragraphs: Context-based offline meta-reinforcement learning aims to train a shared policy that can handle multiple tasks using representations learned from existing data. The task representation tells the policy which situation it should adapt to. This paper asks whether several established approaches to learning these representations can be understood through one underlying objective.

The authors show that the examined methods optimize approximate bounds on the same mutual information between a task variable and its latent representation. In plain terms, they encourage the representation to retain information that identifies the task. This connection explains apparently different algorithms through a shared information-theoretic framework and provides room to design alternative approximations.

The paper demonstrates that flexibility through supervised and self-supervised implementations of the objective. Experiments report strong generalization across reinforcement learning benchmarks, context shifts, data quality levels, and neural architectures. These results support the framework as both an explanatory account and an algorithm-design tool. The authors also propose its potential as an offline pretraining approach for decision-making foundation models, presenting that broader application as a future possibility.
neurips-2024-towards-an-information-theo.tldr: The paper unifies context-based offline meta-RL methods through task–representation mutual information and develops supervised and self-supervised implementations.

paragraphs: Most vision-language interactions require a user to prompt each response. Live coaching introduces another requirement: a system must monitor an unfolding activity and decide when feedback is useful. This paper uses fitness coaching to study that form of asynchronous interaction in a real-world setting that is challenging but controlled.

The authors introduce the QEVD dataset and benchmark. Models must recognize complex human actions, identify possible mistakes, and provide suitable feedback in real time. Success therefore depends on both message content and timing. Recognizing an action alone is insufficient for the benchmark's broader goal of delivering relevant guidance during the activity.

Experiments reveal limitations in existing state-of-the-art vision-language models on these interaction demands. The authors respond with a simple end-to-end streaming baseline that can react asynchronously to human actions with appropriate feedback at an appropriate moment. The contribution combines an evaluation setting with a concrete baseline, making proactive response timing part of the modeling problem alongside visual understanding and language generation.
neurips-2024-what-to-say-and-when-to-say.tldr: QEVD evaluates real-time fitness coaching, and a streaming baseline addresses the joint challenge of choosing useful feedback and delivering it at the right time.
